prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1140; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant's attorney confirmed representation today and asked that all contact go through their office. Received the initial loss notice describing a left turn collision at an intersection, with the claimant reporting neck pain after the impact.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted with the first report. They show the rear-quarter damage and the front-end damage on the other vehicle in the places one would expect from the described impact, and the vehicle damage lines up with the account given. The driver is named on the policy and the police report places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant through counsel. The account matched what was told at first notice, with the same sequence and the same description of the turn, and no new details came up. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos and the police report are carrying most of the weight on the crash details.

Entry 4: Pulled the vehicle history. No earlier damage to this vehicle is on record, and nothing indicates the damage predates the coverage start. Also noted a minor neck strain treated years ago that healed fully and was not connected to the current complaint, which I will need to clarify with the treating provider.

Entry 5: Treatment records received. The care followed a usual course for this kind of soft tissue injury, with the frequency of visits tapering as the patient's symptoms improved. The reported whiplash fits the kind and force of the impact.

Entry 6: Summary: the injury, the damage, and the claimant's account are consistent with one another and with the police report. Recommend moving to evaluation of the bodily injury claim under counsel's demand, pending receipt of the prior treatment records.
